summary: TrainMate (train-companion social app): users create journeys (train_number + travel_date + coach + route + college/gender), get matched to other users on the exact same train/date, send pending companion requests, accept/reject them, and accepted companions get a conversation. Blocking and reporting exist as moderation features. Matching SQL is only train_number==train_number && travel_date==travel_date (coach/college/gender/route are client-side display/filters only). Request lifecycle in the DB uses only 'pending'|'accepted'|'rejected' (cancellation = hard DELETE of the row; there is no 'cancelled'/'declined' status). Accepted companions become conversations by inserting directly into the `conversations` table (RLS gate via can_create_conversation/users_share_journey DB functions; the frontend never calls these RPCs directly). Profiles: avatar flow = file -> image crop (ImageCropModal) -> 5MB/type validation -> upload to private 'avatars' bucket -> 1-year signed URL stored on profiles.avatar_url -> cache-busted at render via ?t= timestamp. Blocking inserts into blocked_users(blocker_id, blocked_id); filtering of blocked users from matches/requests is delegated to RLS (is_blocked DB function) — the frontend fetches blockedUsers but never actually filters the matches list with it (it appears only in the effect's dependency array). Reporting inserts into user_reports(reporter_id, reported_id, reason) with an optional free-text reason (no category enum). Note: can_view_journey, can_create_conversation, and is_blocked exist only as generated-type RPC signatures / Postgres RLS helpers; none is invoked from the React code (the only RPC call in scope-adjacent code is soft_delete_conversation in useChat).
businessRules: Request status values (DB column `requests.status`): only 'pending' | 'accepted' | 'rejected'. requestStatusSchema in validations.ts = z.enum(['pending','accepted','rejected']). There is NO 'cancelled' or 'declined' status.

Frontend derived UI statuses (RequestStatus in useRequests): 'none' | 'outgoing_pending' | 'incoming_pending' | 'accepted' | 'rejected'. getRequestStatus computes these from the DB status + request direction.

Cancelling a request = hard DELETE of the row (useRequests.cancelRequest: .delete().eq('id', requestId)), not a status transition. After cancel the other user can no longer see the request and a new request can be sent.
A 'rejected' request can be re-sent: renderActionButton shows 'Send Request' for both 'rejected' and 'none' statuses (rejection does not create a cooldown or block).
Request direction: sender = from_user_id, receiver = to_user_id. 'incoming_pending' means to_user_id === current user; 'outgoing_pending' means from_user_id === current user.
Accepting (incoming) updates requests.status to 'accepted' (.eq('id', requestId)); the recipient is the one allowed to accept/reject in the UI. Rejecting updates status to 'rejected'.

On accept from the Requests page, a conversation is immediately created and the user is navigated to /chat/:id. On accept from the Matched page, ONLY the status is updated; the conversation is created lazily when the user clicks Chat.

Expired-request cleanup: on Requests page mount, any request where current user is the sender (from_user_id), status='pending', and travel_date < (today - 2 days) is hard-deleted. Only sender-side expired requests are cleaned.

Journey matching SQL: journeys.select('*').eq('train_number', X).eq('travel_date', Y).neq('user_id', currentUser). Matching is EXACT train_number + EXACT travel_date only; coach, college, gender, boarding/destination station are NOT part of the match query — they are displayed and filtered client-side on the Matched page.
A journey is not matchable once 'past' (getJourneyStatus(travel_date) === 'past' blocks findCompanionsForJourney with a toast). 'today' journeys ARE still matchable.

Journey status computed in frontend from travel_date vs local today (midnight-normalized): equal => 'today', less => 'past', greater => 'upcoming'. Active tab shows today + upcoming (today first); Past tab shows past.

Unverified train rule: if the autocomplete did not verify the train (isVerified=false), the raw entry is INSERTED into unverified_trains(train_number, train_name, submitted_by, entered_value, normalized_value=lowercase trimmed) AND the journey is still created anyway (unverified entry does not block journey creation).

Journey form validation (journeySchema): name 1..100; trainNumber 1..20 and regex /^[A-Za-z0-9\s-]+$/; travelDate cannot be in the past (>= local today); coach max 10 optional; boarding/destination 1..100; college max 200 optional; gender enum ['male','female','other','prefer-not-to-say',''] optional.

getRequestStatus(otherUserId, trainNumber, travelDate): matches a request only when both directions of the pair match AND, when train/date args are provided, train_number===trainNumber && travel_date===travelDate. If no train/date given it returns the FIRST request between the pair regardless of journey.

Avatar upload pipeline: validate image/* + <=5MB -> ImageCropModal crop -> new File(croppedBlob,'avatar.jpg',image/jpeg) -> storage.remove([`${user.id}/avatar.jpg`]) then upload with upsert to private 'avatars' bucket -> createSignedUrl(path, 365 days) -> profiles.update({avatar_url: signedUrl}). Rendered with cache-buster ?t=avatarVersion; refreshAvatar() bumps avatarVersion after upload.

Blocking: blocked_users.insert({blocker_id: user.id, blocked_id}) to block; delete eq blocker_id+blocked_id to unblock. Frontend fetches blocked_id list per blocker but does NOT filter the Matched list client-side (blockedUsers only appears in the filter effect's deps, not the body) — enforcement is delegated to RLS via the is_blocked DB function.
Reporting: user_reports.insert({reporter_id: user.id, reported_id, reason: reason.trim() || null}). Reason is optional free-text; no reason category enum is captured.

TrainAutocomplete search: trains.select('train_number, train_name').eq('active', true).or(train_number ilike %q%, train_name ilike %q%).limit(15), debounced 300ms, minimum 2 chars. Selecting a suggestion sets isVerified=true; typing free text sets isVerified=false.

Profiles of OTHER users never expose email: ProfileModal selects only name, college, gender, bio, hobbies, avatar_url (deliberately excludes email). Own email is shown from the auth session (user.email), not from profiles.

Edit profile saves only: name (required, trimmed), bio (trimmed or null), hobbies (trimmed or null), college (trimmed or null), gender (enum or null). avatar_url is only changed through the avatar upload path.

Conversation creation inserts participants (array), participant_names (json object keyed by user id), train_number, travel_date, last_message='', last_message_time=now. Reuse logic: Matched page reuses an existing conversation when both participant ids are in the loaded conversations list before creating a new one.
Message validation (messageSchema): text trim 1..2000 chars. Text message sends also bump conversations.last_message (substring 255) and last_message_time.

supabaseCalls: profiles.select('id, name, bio, hobbies, college, gender, avatar_url').eq('id', user.id).single()
profiles.update(updates).eq('id', user.id)  [name, bio, hobbies, college, gender, avatar_url]
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Own profile loaded into state; PGRST116 (no row) tolerated as null profile. updateProfile merges into local state. Email is NOT selected from profiles (comes from auth session).

dataFlows.uiBehavior: Full profile merged over the journey-card stub; email deliberately omitted. Hobbies rendered as badges split on comma; gender 'prefer_not_to_say' formatted to 'Prefer not to say'; Same College / Same Coach badges computed case-insensitively/exactly.

dataFlows.uiBehavior: Validates image/* type and <=5MB, opens crop modal; on crop complete previews blob, uploads as avatar.jpg, shows spinner, refreshAvatar() bumps cache-buster, refetches profile, toasts success; on failure restores previous avatar_url.

supabaseCalls: profiles.update({name, bio, hobbies, college, gender}).eq('id', user.id)
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Name required (client-side check before submit); empty bio/hobbies/college coerced to null; gender select uses 'prefer_not_to_say' (underscore) value; toasts and closes on success.

supabaseCalls: unverified_trains.insert({train_number, train_name, submitted_by, entered_value, normalized_value: lower+trim})  [only when isTrainVerified === false]
journeys.insert({user_id, user_name, train_number, train_name, travel_date, coach, boarding_station, destination_station, college, gender}).select().single()
dataFlows.uiBehavior: journeySchema.safeParse gates submission (first error toasts). On success form resets, dialog closes, and findCompanionsForJourney(data) is invoked immediately (auto-navigates to /matched).

Journeys categorized into today/past/upcoming by travel_date vs local midnight. Bell badge shows count of incoming pending requests. Active tab = today+upcoming, Past tab = past. Delete requires AlertDialog confirm then journeys.delete().eq('id').

dataFlows.trigger: Dashboard: Find Companions on a journey card
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Aborts with toast if journey is past. Formats matches into Match objects (id,userId,userName,trainNumber,trainName,travelDate,coach,boardingStation,destinationStation,college,gender), writes localStorage 'journeyData' + 'matches', toasts count, navigates to /matched.

Shows suggestion dropdown (keyboard nav: arrows/Enter/Escape, click-outside close). Selecting suggestion sets verified=true and fires onChange(train_number, train_name, true). Free text marks isVerified=false and shows 'Train not found in database. Entry will be saved for review.' warning.

Loads journey + matches from localStorage. Applies client-side filters: coach exact, college substring (case-insensitive), gender exact, sameCollege exact-case-insensitive vs own college, sameCoach exact vs own coach. No-journey state shows EmptyState with 'Go to Dashboard'.

supabaseCalls: requests.insert({from_user_id, from_name: journeyData.name, to_user_id, to_name, train_number, travel_date, boarding_station, destination_station, status: 'pending'})
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Button disabled while sending. On success toasts 'Request sent' and re-fetches requests (getRequestStatus then flips the button to disabled 'Requested'). from_email/to_email are NOT populated.

dataFlows.trigger: Matched: Accept on an incoming pending match
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Toasts 'You can now chat with...' and re-fetches requests. No conversation created here; the Chat button appears and creates the conversation lazily.

dataFlows.trigger: Matched: Chat button on an accepted match
supabaseCalls: conversations.insert({participants:[user.id,match.userId], participant_names:{user.id:name, match.userId:userName}, train_number, travel_date, last_message:'', last_message_time}).select().single()  [only if no existing conversation with both participants]
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Reuses existing conversation when both participant ids found; otherwise creates one. Navigates to /chat/:conversationId with state {otherUser, trainNumber, travelDate}.

supabaseCalls: conversations.insert({participants:[user.id, request.from_user_id], participant_names, train_number, travel_date, last_message:'', last_message_time}).select().single()
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Accepts, builds display names (own from profile or 'You', other from from_name or 'User'), creates the conversation, navigates to /chat/:id with otherUser {id, from_name, from_email}. If conversation creation fails after accept, toasts 'Request accepted but failed to create chat. Go to Chats to start messaging.'

dataFlows.trigger: Requests page: reject incoming / cancel outgoing
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Reject toasts 'Request rejected' and updates local list. Cancel requires AlertDialog confirm ('This will withdraw your travel companion request. You can send a new request later.') then hard-deletes the row and removes it from local state.
Logs 'Cleaned up N expired request(s)'. Runs once per mount; only sender-side pending requests older than travel_date+2 days removed.

Adds id to local blockedUsers list, toasts 'You will no longer see this user in matches.', closes modal. No explicit re-filter of the matches list (blockedUsers is in the filter effect deps but unused in its body).

supabaseCalls: user_reports.insert({reporter_id: user.id, reported_id, reason: reason.trim() || null})
dataFlows.uiBehavior: Opens ReportDialog with free-text reason (optional). Submit toasts 'Report submitted' and resets reason; failure toasts error.

supabaseCalls: messages.insert({conversation_id, sender_id, sender_name, text, attachment_url, attachment_type, attachment_name, attachment_size})
last_read.upsert({user_id, conversation_id, timestamp}, onConflict 'user_id,conversation_id')  [mark as read]
dataFlows.uiBehavior: messageSchema validates text (1..2000); attachment skips schema but enforces 2000-char cap. Live INSERT subscription via postgres_changes appends messages. last_read channel updates read receipts. (Conversations list re-fetched on any conversations change.)

edgeCases: can_view_journey, can_create_conversation, is_blocked, can_view_profile, is_conversation_participant, users_share_journey exist as Supabase RPC signatures in types.ts but are NEVER called from React. They are Postgres RLS helpers; enforcement is server-side. The only RPC the frontend actually invokes (chat scope) is soft_delete_conversation.

Blocked users are not filtered out of the Matched list client-side: the filter effect depends on blockedUsers but never references it in the body, so a blocked match still renders until RLS hides their journey row on the next match query.
Rejected requests allow re-sending (no cooldown/flag). Cancelled requests disappear entirely (hard delete), so the pair can immediately re-request.

getRequestStatus without train/date returns the FIRST request between the pair regardless of journey, so on the Matched page a request from a DIFFERENT train/date could surface as the status for the current journey if the caller passes undefined train/date (Matched always passes journeyData train/date, so this is mitigated there).
cleanupExpiredRequests only prunes requests the current user SENT (from_user_id) — incoming expired pending requests from others are never cleaned by this hook.

Dashboard coach values differ from Matched filter values: journey form uses '1A','2A','3A','3E','EC','CC','SL','2S','UR/GN'; Matched coach filter dropdown uses 'S1','B1','A1','2A','3A','SL','CC','2S'. Filter values like S1/B1/A1 never appear in the journeys form, so those coach filters would rarely match.

Gender value inconsistency: Dashboard journey form stores 'prefer-not-to-say' (hyphen, matches journeySchema); EditProfileModal stores 'prefer_not_to_say' (underscore) into profiles. Both ProfileModal and ViewProfileModal format 'prefer_not_to_say'; only ProfileModal/ViewProfile handle it — the hyphenated variant is not specially formatted.

Avatar upload filename uses the raw file extension (e.g. .png, .jpg from file.name), while EditProfileModal always creates the cropped File named 'avatar.jpg' with image/jpeg — so the stored path extension depends on the upload path used (cropped path is always .jpg).
A train typed manually that EXISTS in the trains table but is not selected from suggestions is still treated as unverified (isVerified=false) and logged to unverified_trains.
Journey insert allows duplicate journeys (same user, same train/date) — no dedup; multiple identical journey rows are permitted.
Journeys on 'today' are still matchable (only 'past' is blocked), meaning a user can still find companions on the day of travel.
profiles.select for own profile tolerates PGRST116 (missing row) by setting profile to null without error; all other read paths (fetchUserProfile, ProfileModal) return null/merge gracefully on error.

If a user accepts a request but the conversation insert fails (e.g. RLS can_create_conversation denied), the request remains 'accepted' and the user is routed to the Chats list instead of the chat — an accepted companion with no conversation is possible.
localStorage journeyData/matches become stale if the user changes journeys without re-planning; navigating to /matched outside the Dashboard flow shows 'No journey data found'.
Report reason has no length or content validation and no category; empty reason is stored as NULL.
Blocked/unblocked are not mirrored to the requests table — a blocked user's existing accepted conversations/requests are not cleaned by the frontend.
Emails on requests (from_email/to_email) are declared in the Request interface but never written by the frontend insert, so they remain null.
notes: Tables read/written: profiles (read own + others, update name/bio/hobbies/college/gender/avatar_url; email never written/read from this table), journeys (insert/list/delete/match by user, train_number, travel_date), requests (insert pending; update to accepted/rejected; delete to cancel; select all involving user; count incoming pending; cleanup sender-side expired), blocked_users (insert/delete/select blocked_id by blocker_id), user_reports (insert reporter_id/reported_id/reason), trains (read active for autocomplete), unverified_trains (insert unverified train entries), conversations (insert + select contains participant; update last_message/last_message_time), messages (insert, live subscribe INSERT), last_read (upsert/select). Storage buckets: 'avatars' (private, 1-year signed URL stored on profile; cache-busted with ?t=) and 'chat-attachments' (private, 1-year signed URL). RLS helper functions referenced by generated types (can_view_journey, can_create_conversation, can_view_profile, is_blocked, is_blocked_in_conversation, is_conversation_participant, users_share_journey, soft_delete_conversation) are not invoked from the React code in scope; RLS is the enforcement layer for journey visibility and conversation creation. Files analyzed: useProfile.ts, useRequests.ts, useBlockedUsers.ts, Dashboard.tsx, Matched.tsx, Requests.tsx, ProfileModal.tsx, EditProfileModal.tsx, ViewProfileModal.tsx, TrainAutocomplete.tsx, ReportDialog.tsx, validations.ts (plus useChat.tsx and supabase types.ts for the conversation/RPC context).
